# C has no enum type, so NoEnum makes each member the int its ordinal is, and
# `var maybe option[Status] = active` wraps that int in an option of Status.
# C took it for a conversion it had no rule for ("converting int to
# option[Status]"). FuzzPipeline found it.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

enum Status { active, inactive, pending }

component panel ui.node {
    var maybe option[Status] = active
    var none option[Status] = null

    ui.text #shown(value=maybe == active ? "on" : "off")
    ui.button #off(text="off", @click { maybe = Status.inactive })
}

func testOptionOfEnum(t test.Test, c panel) {
    t.assert(c.maybe == active)
    t.assert(c.none == null)
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "on")
    c.off.click()
    t.assert(c.maybe == inactive)
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "off")
}

ui.window {
    panel
}
